For the low price it's definitely worth buying.
It will frustrate you immensely at the beginning, you will get slapped around, die and repeat the process.
But, after the combat system clicks, it is extremely satisfying and fun. You will be enjoying yourself exploring dank dungeons and gearing up or fighting in the arena and climbing ranks. It's tense and difficult but very rewarding. The game is also super pretty - gear you find is detailed and locations are super detailed and immersive - even though it's some godforsaken dungeon, it looks lived in, and built with purpose.
As a point of criticism - update cycle is extremely slow, for a long time I was left with an impression that the game is dead and abandoned. Nevertheless, the update came and the quality of existing content is impressive.
I recommend it.

The game is awesome, and the combat is very satisfying once you get the hang of it. The magic system is great, and lore-wise looks quite well thought out, and there are some cool spells you can utilise in the campaign(Revelation perk, take it).

The worldbuilding looks interesting; there are lore scrolls everywhere, some hidden rooms with loot and a physics system that you have to use to get to the coolest stuff. You can also mess with enemies by making barricades, making them trip with objects, throwing them with force thaumaturgy, getting around with the help of planks, etc.

The pace of updates so far was glacial, but I hope they'll be able to speed things up now, as a lot of the systems they worked on were introduced.

If you want to have a decent fun time and don't want to go for the roguelike experience of the main story, select the arena. You'll see a lot of fun combat and some cool enemies, and also be able to master the combat(no magic there though).

Exanima jest tworzona na autorskim silniku. Jest to ten sam silnik zapowiedziany aż 14 LAT TEMU do gry Sui Generis. Jednak jak sami autorzy piszą, Exanima to ta sama gra co Sui Generis - wszystkie mechaniki i silnik tworzone są z myślą o tej drugiej, znacznie większej grze. Do tego studio składa się raptem z kilku pracowników i jest dobrym przykładem gry Indie, która ma być dopracowana do perfekcji.

Rys świata gry.

Otóż zostajemy wrzuceni przez bandytów do podziemia. Świat na powierzchni wydaje się zwyczajnym miejscem, jednak wraz z zagłębianiem się w kolejne poziomy podziemia dowiadujemy się coraz ciekawszych rzeczy - dlaczego w podziemiu wałęsają się nieumarli, kto za to odpowiada i znacznie więcej.
O samym uniwersum dowiadujemy się z porozrzucanych książek oraz listów pisanych przez poprzednie osoby odwiedzające lub zamieszkujące te miejsce. (Uwaga - gra jest wyłącznie w języku angielskim i o ile nie jest przesadnie skomplikowanie napisana, to nie wystarczy znajomość podstaw ang.)

Dodatkowo dysponujemy "tutorialową areną" do nauki walki oraz pełnoprawną arenę, w której prowadzimy kompanię gladiatorów toczących pojedynki na powierzchni. I ta część gry jest również bardzo dopracowana.

Trzeba napisać również, że gra jest całkowicie oparta na fizyce - każdy ruch, atak, unik jest bazowany na obiektach - jeśli broń trafi w cel, mamy trafienie - dużo zależy też od miejsca trafienia, siły uderzenia czy samej broni. Oberwanie dwuręcznym młotem w nieosłoniętą głowę często kończy się natychmiastową śmiercią, zaś trafienie mieczem w pełną zbroję płytową nie powoduje prawie żadnych konsekwencji.

Gra na początku może wydawać się bardzo trudna - nad sterowaniem należy solidnie popracować, ale efekty dają niezwykłą frajdę. Mi to zajęło kilka dobrych godzin lata temu.

W głównej części gry mamy do wyboru dwie "klasy" postaci - Wieśniaka - bez żadnych specjalnych umiejętności oraz "Nieznanego" - "Unknown" - osobę z zanikiem pamięci, która dysponuje pewnego rodzaju magicznym potencjałem - i przede wszystkim to tą postacią powinniśmy zacząć grać.
W trakcie, po pokonaniu mini-bossa odblokowujemy kolejną postać, która potrafi walczyć i ma niewielki potencjał magiczny.

"Magia", czy też "Taumaturgia" jak jest nazwana w grze dzieli się na 5 odłamów - obecnie w grze dostępne są 2, a trzecią szkołę możemy odblokować pod koniec gry. 
Poza tym, dysponujemy sporą liczbą umiejętności walki, korzystania z pancerzy, tarczy i dwoma gałęziami mentalnymi wspierającymi magię. W wersji 1.0 otrzymamy również walkę dystansową.

Exanima is a perfect example of a unique idea ruined by terrible execution.

Yes, the concept is interesting. Physics-based melee combat, weighty weapons, dark dungeons, realistic movement, and brutal injuries all sound cool. That is the only credit I can give this game. Everything else feels like a mess of bad controls, bad UI, bad onboarding, and bad design decisions pretending to be “hardcore.”

The controls are horrible. The character does not feel realistic. It feels broken. Moving around, fighting, opening doors, picking up items, dragging objects, using keys, managing inventory — almost every basic action feels awkward and annoying. You are not just fighting enemies. You are fighting the game itself every second.

The combat is not “deep” enough to excuse how awful it feels. Sometimes it produces a cool moment, but most of the time it feels like two drunk mannequins swinging metal sticks in a closet. Weapons get caught on everything. Characters stumble around like idiots. Simple actions become a struggle for no good reason.

The UI is absolute garbage, especially in Arena mode. The equipment system is one of the most anti-player systems I have ever seen. Ranks, tiers, loadouts, arsenal storage, merchant trading, manager inventory, fighter inventory — everything is split apart in the most inconvenient way possible. Buying gear should be simple. Comparing gear should be simple. Instead, the game turns it into tedious menu labor.

You cannot even conveniently compare merchant items with the equipment your fighter is actually using in a specific tier loadout. You have to run between merchant screens and management menus like you are doing clerical work in a badly designed spreadsheet. That is not hardcore. That is trash UI.

The game explains almost nothing. It throws important mechanics at you with barely any guidance and expects you to dig through wikis, Reddit posts, Steam discussions, and old forum replies just to understand basic systems. Injuries, healing, red health, skills, arena progression, equipment tiers, keys, combat techniques — the game barely teaches any of it properly.

The friendly AI is awful. Companions block your movement, walk into your attacks, charge into bad positions, get surrounded, and behave like liabilities. Enemy AI, meanwhile, often feels much more aggressive and coordinated. Your allies feel like dead weight, while enemies act like they actually know how to play the game.

This game constantly confuses inconvenience with difficulty. It confuses poor explanation with mystery. It confuses clunky controls with realism. It confuses bad interface design with depth.

Hard games can still have good controls. Hard games can still have readable UI. Hard games can still teach their mechanics. Exanima fails at all of that.

The idea is original. The execution is awful.

This is not a hidden masterpiece. This is a frustrating, clunky, poorly explained mess with one interesting gimmick buried under terrible design. Not recommended.

0.9.5 had serious negative consequences for the fighting. Enemies now have superhuman senses and block all attacks. They block while laying down, they block from behind, their shields can barely be penetrated. This has always been the case but it has been heavily exacerbated by the improvements to the AI. I really love that we have made the AI more challenging, but with parrying in its current state, it has made the experience very frustrating. 

These changes to AI have made the game considerably more challenging but not in a very satisfying way. There also seems to be less variance between the lowest skilled NPC and the highest skilled NPC, whereas before it was very evident if the person you were fighting was skilled or not. Lower difficulty AI are still good at dodging and good at multi-combatant tactics. Getting hits off on my opponents seems to be more luck based at this point (though it is still a little easier to hit fighters below adept difficulty). Before patch - I had multiple arena saves with 10+ tournament armors which is moderately skilled at the game. But now, most enemies feel like they have the tournament AI which was noticeably stronger before this patch.

The changes they are considering for parrying, new stances, and a bash mechanic would largely resolve these issues, but the critical point is how long it'll take for them to implement these changes. I hope they're able to add these additions soon. Before 0.9.5, this was one of my favorite games of all-time. They made a lot of other improvements in other areas not related to combat; unfortunately, combat is the most important aspect of the game in my opinion as it is the main driving force for everything that happens. 

Also, they changed the physics engine which I was initially excited for. But enemies can no longer be hit so hard that they fly a short distance. They kinda just crumple and fall over in a more realistic manner. While more realistic, I can't deny that smacking enemies around was extremely fun and it was always hilarious to see how far an enemy could be tossed with a pitchfork.

The game is cool in concept, and I think the attempt is nice, but the game is ultimately very wonky. It is not for everyone; it's really only for people who end up REALLY liking it. I think the fanbase has somewhat forgotten that this game is aspiring to one day be an RPG like many others - and I think it is naive to suggest it is going to succeed at doing this, at the rate and concept Exanima is working with. The controls aren't very good and the combat is ultimately wonky like gang-beasts. You can spend an incredible amount of time attempting to master the controls, and even then the combat will always be/feel wonky anyways. I've gotten to the point where I'm proficient at the game, but it is consistently very inconsistent despite this. It can be really frustrating sometimes. It is a hyper-niche game like Half-Sword with, in my opinion worse execution, but has an incredible atmosphere and a very slow but fun dungeon campaign. Albeit the lack of saves after level 3 is utterly insane and masochistic - the creator seems to be insistent on this which I find to be unwise at best. I somewhat feel the game refuses to change or learn from similar games because of some sunken cost fallacy. Just my thoughts. There are others who have the same feelings as I do, but expressed more concretely and frankly far more biting than mine. A lot of wasted potential I fear is happening with this game right now, but people are blinded by the romance of the stoic, ignorant pressing onwards despite criticism the devs seem to have.

Upsides:
+ Very interesting fighting mechanic that I haven't seen anywhere implemented so well. Most people end up not liking it though
+ The arena, genuenly entertaining
+ Realistic good looking items, good optimisation
+ Layered armour system
+ The weapons are well made, their shape and size, everything about them matters and makes you change how you fight
+ The awsome floor with caves. THIS IS WHAT THIS GAME HAD TO BE.

Downsides:
The arena is a mess where you train to fight, while the dungeon, the main focus of the game has NOTHING interesting AND IT DISCOURAGES FIGHTING. See the irony? Anyways, each room is a useless box of useless wooden junk, majority of floors are copy paste, so you'll drop the game from boredom and frustration before seeing something different. Because the layout is disorienting and uninspiring, the architecture is tame and tells very little, and there's no way to use paper, pencils or chalk you can find in order to help navigate and you need keys to progress! The keys are very tiny and are impossible to notice unless you know where they are, but then it means there is nothing for you to explore if you already know where everything is! All this together creates a gameplay where you run around the same rooms and corridors for hours, utterly lost, trying to find a very small key, again, FOR HOURS. Just running around. Nothing else. Finished the floor? Good. Here's another absolutely the same floor with same keys that are somewhere god knows where. It's infuriating obviously! WHY, why would you design a game like this? But that's not all: the fights in dungeon are the only interesting and exciting bits. They also just happen to be so ruthless that you'll do anything to avoid said fights because it's very easy to get injured and there's no way to heal except for potions, around 4? in the whole game, and they are hard to find. And their location is randomised. 

This game is the example of realism driving the gameplay to such a realistic point it's unplayable. Yes, there's lots of upsides, but in the end it doesn't matter if the dungeon is so bad.  Of course realistically combat is hazardous and it's best to avoid fighting. Of course realistically there's nothing interesting in an old dungeon. Of course realistically it's hard to find keys and progress in an abandoned dungeon. BUT THAT'S NOT WHY WE PLAY GAMES!!!!!!!!

Exanima is a unique experience that is particularly fun if you are into gear setup, armor layering and space based combat with a lot of control. The areas are interesting and the dungeon is carefully designed and varied, but know you are stepping into a world of annoyance for one reason: Parkour.

This game does not save. You get one final checkpoint a third through the game and if you die after that its back to the start. The game's combat is designed for this, you have healing and fights are rarely fatal, you get knocked out and often have another chance. Armor reduces permanent damage. These all make sense and fit the flow, combat is dangerous, but reasonably able to be approached with careful preperation.

But why, oh why, is every single pitfall an instant death with no recourse? And why, oh why, Bare Mettle, do you have our character prancing on the edge of platforms so often with dozens of hours on the line to be wiped out with a single missed input? I love playing Exanima. But the floor scares me ten times more than the fights do. The risk/reward is completely out of line. The platforming sections Ill fit the game, especially the instant death part.

I would very much recommend to the developers of this game for pits in these sections to send you down a floor to a temporary area you have to leave, causing heavy damage in the process. Anything except an instant game over. Mario-esque deaths do not fit a game where saves are dozens of hours long.

С одной стороны, Exanima — реально интересная игра: огромные уровни-лабиринты, необычная физика, глубокая боёвка, куча секретов, интересный лор, отлично проработанная система экипировки и т.д.

С другой стороны:

1. Хочется повертеть на детородном органе эти гигантские уровни-лабиринты без сохранений. Всё тёмное, нихрена не видно, персонаж может споткнуться на ровном месте и улететь в яму, туда же может навернуться компаньон, можно где-нибудь застрять и т.п. Да, это обходится бэкапами сейвов, но это костыль.

2. Невозможность нормально зафиксировать камеру за спиной персонажа в бою — отдельный вид пытки. Для этого надо постоянно зажимать дополнительную кнопку. Играю в Exanima уже много лет урывками и каждый раз не могу привыкнуть к боёвке.
Вне боя всё удобно: бегаешь с зажатой ПКМ — всё отлично.
В бою же начинается цирк:
- двигаешься на WASD;
- персонаж поворачивается на курсор;
- курсором надо рисовать замахи;
- одновременно рулить движением персонажа для увеличения силы удара;
- держать курсор около противника для блока/парирования;
- ещё и постоянно выравнивать камеру отдельной кнопкой.
В итоге всё это превращается в эпилептические пируэты и полную дезориентацию на экране.

3. Баланс тоже местами сомнительный. Чем ниже спускаешься, тем сильнее начинают сосать режущее оружие и т.п.: кучи скелетов, бронированные враги, сраные големы и т.д.
Големы тупо душные - обычно убиваешь через дверные проемы (оружием махать нормально не могут) или прижав к стенке (опять же не могут махать оружием).

4. Разработка идёт сверхмедленно. Интервал между последними крупными обновлениями — чуть ли не по 3 года.

Лично у меня главная причина дропов — именно управление в бою. На верхних уровнях схватки ещё короткие и не так бесят, но на нижних бои затяжные, и управление успевает натурально вымотать.

Is this game in Early Access since ages?

Yeah.

Is this game getting regular updates?

No, but recently yes, and you got updates about the development monthly.

Did the team deliver?

Absolutely.

Exanima is actually meant as a teaster demo type of thing for a much more vast game, Sui Generis, but the game will need a completely new engine because it does things other games didn't at the time it was created. (now we got some physics based sword fighting games, but Exanima is different)

Exanima could be best described as physics based, story and exploration driven top down/third person immersive sim dungeon crawler, but no term like that delivers the feeling the game gives you.

I can only recommend it, but it will not please every player, it is a bit of a niche game.
